title: C++
subtitle: Modern C++ from a first program to professional practice: value semantics, RAII, templates, the standard library, concurrency and the tools that keep large codebases correct.
description: C++ is a compiled, statically typed language that gives you two things at once: direct control over memory and the machine, and abstractions (classes, templates, the standard library) that cost nothing at run time when you do not use them. It runs inside web browsers, game engines, databases, compilers, trading systems, robots, scientific simulations and the cores of machine-learning frameworks. It is also large, old and full of sharp edges, so this course teaches **modern C++** (C++20 and C++23) as experienced engineers write it today, and is honest about the parts that still bite.

The course assumes the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are. No C is required. It takes you from compiling your first program through references, classes, RAII, move semantics, templates and concepts, containers and ranges, to error handling, undefined behaviour and sanitizers, threads and atomics, CMake and package managers, and a complete small project. Every complete program in the lessons was compiled with GCC 14 (`g++ -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra`) and run, and the output shown is the output it printed.

To run the programs, install a C++ compiler: [GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/) (on Linux, from your distribution; on Windows, through MSYS2 or WSL), [Clang](https://clang.llvm.org/) (on macOS, `xcode-select --install`), or [Visual Studio](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/) with the *Desktop development with C++* workload on Windows. C++ has no official online playground; the community's standard one is [Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/), which compiles and runs code with dozens of compilers in your browser and shows the machine code they produce.

levels.title: The core language
levels.summary: How C++ programs are compiled and linked, values, references and const, functions, overloading and lambdas, and classes whose destructors clean up after them (RAII).

levels.title: Ownership, generic code and the standard library
levels.summary: Move semantics and smart pointers, templates constrained by concepts, and the containers, iterators, algorithms and ranges of the standard library.

levels.title: Correctness, concurrency and real projects
levels.summary: Exceptions and std::expected, undefined behaviour and the sanitizers that find it, threads, mutexes and atomics, and a complete project built with CMake, a package manager and the C++ Core Guidelines.
